PRISONER OF WAR. A printed transport list in the Pretoria government archives, image group 008019246, carries THREE CONSECUTIVE BOOYZENS shipped on the CITY OF CAMBRIDGE on 3 JUNE 1901, all entered from PRETORIA: 18463 STEPHANUS FRANCOIS, 28 · 18464 PETRUS JACOBUS, 29 · 18465 DAVID SCHALK, 54. Consecutive numbers on one transport means taken together. Age 54 against a birth of 9 June 1848, which would have made him 52 and six days short of 53 when the ship sailed. THE FULLER REGISTER WAS THEN FOUND, and it is better than the De List in every respect: item 1 of the same film, image 126, gives all three as living at PRETORIA, riding with the PRETORIA COMMANDO, and TAKEN AT TOLOSBERG ON 25 APRIL 1901. Its ages are 26, 27 and 53, which match this archive's own dates where the De List's 28, 29 and 54 did not. If it is him, he was a Transvaal burgher in arms at fifty-two, taken and deported, and he came back — he remarried at Pretoria in November 1905. Fourth on the 1863 list, and THE DIRECT ANCESTOR'S BROTHER — Willem Hermanus is sixth on the same list. For the whole of this project he was a line on that list and nothing else. His wife's 1900 death notice gives him a household: married ELIZABETHA MARGARETHA MARAIS at LADY GREY, the same small Cape church where his brother married Kathleen Barry in 1879; eight children; and by 1900 he was at Pretoria, living in a zinc building in Market Street. He signed her notice there in March 1904 — and on 27 NOVEMBER 1905 he married again at Pretoria, to JOHANNA ELENA STOLS, widow Lowies, of Skinners Court. He was 56, a widower of GOEDE HOOP, PRETORIA, and the register gives his birthplace as CRADOCK. The Remarks column cites his remarriage certificate from the Master, NO. 4795 — which is the number of his first wife’s death notice, so the two documents point at each other and the identification needs no inference. His own death is still not found.

A JGL BOOYZEN countersigned the money papers of a farm school at KWAGGAFONTEIN, DISTRICT MARICO, through 1898 and into 1899: the subsidy application, the book orders, all four quarterly returns, the writing-off of a £61-6-0 deficit, and a letter arguing that the government had paid £8 too little. Death notice 6167 — the oldest Booyzen estate paper in the Cape Master's series, and a generation older in form than anything else this archive has read. Widow of Charles du Plessis; one daughter, married to Benjamin Solomon; “no property whatever except a Bond amounting per balance to £15”. Line 3 answers “both dead”. She is here because she was born in 1754 and died in 1843 — the only two dates this archive has for Magdelena Elisabeth de Beer, both off the family tree with no source stated — and because somebody will one day find her and decide she is the same woman. She is not. Her name is not Magdelena, not Elisabeth, and not de Beer.

BOOYZEN — GEB. 29 DES. 1904 — OORL. 7 JUNIE 1937 — NA DIE KRUIS DIE KROON.” Dead at thirty-two. AND ONE WORD OF IT DOES REAL WORK: “MY geliefde seun”, not “ONS”. BEYLEVELDT) — GEB. 7 JANUARIE 1855 — OORL. 16 MAART 1937.” The Cape Province civil register carries her under a chain of surnames that is its own biography — BOOYZEN BYLEVELD LANGENBOG BOOYZEN — and gives her born 1857 where the stone says 1855. Her Cape probate names her husband as JOHANNES HENDRIK. She died on 16 MARCH 1937, TWELVE WEEKS BEFORE PIETER J. BOOYZEN went into the same ground, and this archive can find no link between them but the surname and the town. SET DOWN SO THAT NOBODY LATER ASSUMES ONE.

people.r: AN EIGHTH CHILD, and one this archive did not have. Confirmed at Indwe on 31 May 1907, aged 21, entered “Booijzen”. A MIJNWERKER of DUGMORE MIJN when he married Susanna Adriana Roodt, 16, at Indwe on 21 September 1908 — the only miner in five generations of read occupations, and the answer to the last line of the family testimony. Two children in nine months by two women of the same surname, both entered “onecht”. His mother stood godmother at the first font, which is how this archive knows whose son he is. AND THEN JOHANNESBURG: a WILLIAM HERMAN BOOYZEN, 47, born Cape Province, married, EX MINER UNDERGROUND, of 62 Langford Street, Booysens, died at Johannesburg Hospital on 29 July 1932 of a perforated duodenal ulcer after about one day, and was buried at BRIXTON on 31 July. The occupation, the province, the age within a year and the cemetery all fit; no parents are named, because a civil registration does not ask. And then the grave register closes it: GRAVE 6889 holds “Boysen, William” and, thirty-six years later, SUSANNA ADRIANA BOOYZEN, buried 29 August 1968 — the woman he married at Indwe in 1908. Husband and wife in one grave.

SIXTEEN when she married at Indwe on 21 September 1908, with her parents consenting, and already the mother of a son born on 31 May. She outlived her husband by thirty-six years and was buried in his grave — number 6889, Johannesburg — on 29 August 1968.

Seventeen at the same confirmation, number 25 on the page to Susanna Adriana’s 26. Mother of the girl born 8 February 1909 — four and a half months after he married the other one. The register names her plainly and this archive does no more than repeat it.

Baptised at Indwe 6 December 1908, entry 15, and entered ONECHT — born four months before his parents married. His godmother was his grandmother, Catharina Maria Sophia Barry. The fourth Willem Hermanus in four generations, and the name still comes from a step-relation with no blood tie.

Baptised at Indwe 22 September 1910, entry 12, entered ONECHT and GRATIS — the fee waived. Named for her godmother Catharina Willemina Levina Buitendag, who stood at both of her father’s children’s fonts.
Godmother at Indwe in 1908 and again in 1910, to two children of the same father by two different mothers — and the second child carries her whole name.
Godfather at both Indwe fonts. A Cornelis de Klerk Roodt, 21, is number 29 in the same 1907 confirmation class; whether they are the same man is not established here.

HIS GRAVE IS READ, and it gives both dates at once. BRENTHURST CEMETERY, BRAKPAN: “IN LIEFDE HERINNERING — AAN ONS VADER — JOHN BARRY BOOYZEN — ★ 26.4.1884 — † 23.1.1952 — RUS SAG.”, cut by Pretoria Grafstene. This archive had “c. 1884” and NO DEATH AT ALL. It now has 26 APRIL 1884 and 23 JANUARY 1952 — the latter matching estate TAB MHG 769/52, a file still unread on a blocked film. “Aan ons vader”: he left children. AND NOW HE HAS A DEATH AND A PLACE. “BOOYZEN JOHN BARRY 1884-1952”, BRENTHURST CEMETERY, BRAKPAN. This archive had him as “c. 1884” with no death at all, and an estate number — TAB MHG 769/52 — on a film that will not open. The stone gives 1884-1952, which matches both the estimate and the estate year, and puts him on the East Rand rather than in Johannesburg. IMAGE LOCATED, NOT YET READ. Eldest son. Present at his father's death in 1905 and the informant — he signs Booyzen four lines under the clerk's Booysen.

Carries the Kolbe name three generations after the 1820 Settler — AND HE HYPHENATED IT. The family tree recorded his wife Maria Jacoba Smit, married 1921, under the compound surname KOLBE-BOOYSEN, and this archive filed that as a tree oddity with nothing behind it. The Eastern Province Herald prints it twice. 16 OCTOBER 1944: “SAWTELLE – KOLBY-BOOYSEN. The engagement has been announced between LEVINA (FINNIE), only daughter of Mr and Mrs D. KOLBE-BOOYSEN, of PORT ELIZABETH, to Raymond Patrick, only son of Mrs D. Sawtelle, of Cambridge, England.” 19 APRIL 1945: “KOLBE-BOOYSEN – KRUGER. To be married at St Cuthbert's Church, Bingley Street, Port Elizabeth… Hilda, only daughter of Lieut. and Mrs F. Kruger of Heidelburg, Transvaal, to WILLIAM (S.A.A.F.), son of Mr and Mrs D. KOLBE-BOOYSEN, of Port Elizabeth.” A TOWN AND TWO CHILDREN, from two notices six months apart — and the engagement spells the headline KOLBY and the body KOLBE, four words from each other.

“Only daughter of Mr and Mrs D. Kolbe-Booysen, of Port Elizabeth.” Her engagement to Raymond Patrick Sawtelle, only son of Mrs D. Sawtelle of Cambridge, England, was announced in the Eastern Province Herald on 16 October 1944, in the last winter of the war. The paper called her FINNIE in brackets, which is the household name and the kind of thing a register never records.

South African Air Force. Married Hilda Kruger — only daughter of Lieut. and Mrs F. Kruger of Heidelberg, Transvaal — at St Cuthbert's Church, Bingley Street, Port Elizabeth, at half past three on the afternoon of Thursday 19 April 1945, three weeks before the war in Europe ended. The notice gives both their service initials and neither of their ages.

people.d: 8 Dec 1956, Florence Nightingale Nursing Home — buried 12 Dec, grave 7110/1
people.r: AND NOW THERE IS A REGISTER. The G2G question this archive posted on 13 September was answered within eighteen hours by PIETER VAN ZYL, who put the baptism on the profile: “South Africa, Dutch Reformed Church Registers (Cape Town Archives)”, ark 1:1:6KPT-T3Z4 — HENRY JAMES BOOŸSEN, BORN 12 AUGUST 1887, BAPTISED 27 NOVEMBER 1887, parents WILLEM HERMANUS BOOŸSEN and CATHARINA MARIA SOPHIA BARRY. Verified here against the index directly. The 12 August 1887 has now travelled from a family tree, to a gravestone, to a church register, in that order, which is the wrong way round and is how it usually goes. THE SAME ANSWER ALSO SAYS he was A CARPENTER WHEN HE MARRIED and A RETIRED MINER OF LANGLAAGTE ESTATES when he died, OF PHTHISIS — and this archive has CORONARY PULMONARY SCLEROSIS off the Johannesburg burial register. Phthisis is the Rand miner’s disease and a retired Langlaagte miner dying of it in 1956 is entirely of a piece; but the two causes are not the same word and this archive has read only one of the two documents. REPORTED ON G2G, NOT VERIFIED HERE. AND HIS STONE SETTLES THE BIRTH. WEST PARK, Johannesburg: “HIER RUS — MY DIERBARE EGGENOOT — HENRY JAMES — GEB. 12.8.1887 — OORL. 8.12.1956 — RUS IN VREDE”, over the surname BOOYZEN. The 12 August 1887 this archive carried marked FROM WIKITREE AND NOT FROM A DOCUMENT is now on his own gravestone, and the death matches the burial register to the day. “My dierbare eggenoot” — the stone was raised by his widow, Dorothea Regina. HIS GRAVE IS PHOTOGRAPHED: “BOOYZEN HENRY JAMES 1887-1956”, WEST PARK CEMETERY, Johannesburg — matching the burial register this archive read and the 12 August 1887 birth WikiTree gives. IMAGE LOCATED, NOT YET READ. A son of Willem Hermanus and Kathleen Barry. WikiTree gives his birth as 12 AUGUST 1887 and his marriage as 17 JUNE 1912 AT ELLIOT, neither of which this archive had—bothFROM WIKITREE, NOT FROM A DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS READ, and the “c. 1887” below is this archive’s own figure, worked back from an age on a burial register. This archive had him as a name on Transvaal estate MHG 10/57 and nothing else — not a birth, not a death. The Johannesburg cemetery register gives all of it: DIED 8 DECEMBER 1956 at the FLORENCE NIGHTINGALE NURSING HOME of CORONARY PULMONARY SCLEROSIS, aged 69, usual residence 3 15TH AVENUE, MAYFAIR — the same suburb where his mother died in 1940 and where his great-niece was married at St Joseph’s in 1949. Buried 12 December in the D.R. section, GRAVE 7110/1, a double plot. In 1912 he married Dorothea Regina Barry, a daughter of his mother's brother Hendrik Nicholaas — the third Barry–Booyzen union in three generations.

people.d: 25 Oct 1918, Turffontein — buried 27 Oct, Brixton, D.R., grave 1119
people.r: TWENTY-FOUR, MARRIED, a SAWYER of 18 Anderson Street, Turffontein — dead of INFLUENZA AND PNEUMONIA after eleven days on 25 October 1918, the centre of Black October, and buried at Brixton on the 27th. Not in this archive before today. Added as a ninth child of Willem Hermanus and Kathleen Barry on three grounds and no document: RICHARD PETER is her own brother's name; a birth about 1894 falls exactly in the gap between her daughter of 1891 and her son of 1901; and his registration gives his birthplace as the CAPE OF GOOD HOPE, which is the migration every one of her children made. A Transvaal death registration names no parents, so this stays INFERRED. And he was NOT A SOLDIER — which kills the best explanation this archive had for his mother's military pension.

people.d: buried 23 Jan 1914, Brixton — D.R. section, grave 2472
people.r: SIX MONTHS OLD — not “0 days”, which is what the index says and what this archive printed for an afternoon. The register keeps Years, Months and Days in three columns and the 6 sits in Months. Hers was a BOUGHT grave, marked Private. The earliest Booyzen burial this archive has found at Brixton, and the beginning of a family plot that would take four more over the next twenty years.
Daughter of Willem Hermanus and Kathleen Barry.

people.d: 1946 — West Park, grave 51, beside her husband
people.r: Baptised at Barkly Oost 24 May 1891, entry 120, named for her mother entire, and fourteen when her father died at Indwe. She married Joseph Heinrich Daschner AT INDWE — the same village — and his 1942 death notice names her “born Booyzen”, with a z, in a Johannesburg typist’s hands. Eleven children, five of them carrying Booyzen and Barry forenames. She died in the Transvaal in 1946 — estate TAB MHG 3734/46, found only when this archive finally searched outside the Cape, and still to be read.

people.d: 19 Apr 1942, Kenilworth — buried 21 Apr, West Park, D.R. section, GRAVE 50 of a double plot 50/51 he bought himself
people.r: Her husband. A PENSIONER (ELECTRICIAN) of 132 Sheffield Street, Kenilworth. Estate TAB MHG 1928/42, filed at Pretoria on 13 May 1942 — the first typewritten document in this archive, and one of only two whose question three names both parents. He had not been married before. She signed the notice: “Surviving Spouse — Saw body after death.”
His father, named on the 1942 death notice — “Deceased”, but named.
His mother, entered on the 1942 death notice as “Sophia Daschner (Stoter)” — the maiden name in brackets, which is what a completed question three looks like.
Eldest daughter, and the third of that name in three generations — Kathleen Barry, then her daughter, then her granddaughter. A major by 1942.

A major by 1942, and now probably a grave: “DASCHNER JOSEPH C. 1911–1992 & ELIZABETH H. 1915–1992”, Rynsoord cemetery, Benoni. He and his wife died the same year. A MATCH ON A NAME AND AN INITIAL, not a document. FROM THE INDEX; no image read.

NAAIRS: “MHG 2703/63 — DASCHNER, WILLIAM HERMAN, 1963”. The stone gives the household name and the year, the estate index gives the registered name and the same year. He was 48. Named for his grandfather Willem Hermanus Booyzen — and so, at four removes, for a step-father with no blood tie to this family at all.
Married a van Deventer; a major by 1942.
A major by 1942.

people.d: buried 20 Jun 1925, Brixton — D.R. section, grave 4410
people.r: THREE MONTHS AND FIVE DAYS old — not “0 days”, which is the index's reading and what this archive printed for an afternoon. The Brixton register keeps Years, Months and Days in three columns. Buried 20 June 1925, D.R. section, grave 4410 — seventeen years before his father went into West Park. A TWELFTH CHILD, and not on the 1942 death notice because he was already dead when it was written. The Johannesburg cemetery index has him buried at Brixton on 20 June 1925, the year he was born. He carries George Downing — the sixth Booyzen or Barry forename to cross into this family, and the one that makes the pattern impossible to read as coincidence. FROM AN INDEX, not from an image; the burial register has not been read.

THE STONE IS NOW READ, and it is the fullest document this archive has for him. SILVERTON, PRETORIA, a double stone under one base reading BOOYZEN: “'n SIMBOOL VAN LIEFDE — AAN MY DIERBARE EGGENOOT EN ONS VADER — STEFANUS FRANCOIS — ✳ 29-9-1874, † 14-5-1940 — Sy plek is leeg, sy stem is stil, ons swyg o'Heer, dit is Gods wil. Ges. 75:1”. HIS BIRTH IS NOW EXACT: 29 SEPTEMBER 1874, where this archive had only “c. October 1874”. And a pillar between the two halves lists TWELVE CHILDREN by their household names — OUBOET · OUSIE · BESSIE · BETIE · HENNA · EVERT · ✝BABA · FANIE · WILLIE · PIETIE · JOHAN · HENNIE — one of them marked dead with a cross. This archive had almost none of them. They are nicknames, not names on a register, and nothing is claimed from them beyond the count. HIS GRAVE IS FOUND AND PHOTOGRAPHED: “BOOYZEN STEFANUS FRANCOIS 1874-1940”, SILVERTON MAIN CEMETERY, PRETORIA — a joint stone with his wife, “BOOYZEN BEATRIX MAGDALENA CATHARINA NEE BOSHOFF 1889-1977”. Both dates match this archive exactly, and hers is the first death year it has had for her. He died at East Lynne, Pretoria, and lies at Silverton. IMAGE LOCATED, NOT YET READ. PRISONER OF WAR. A printed transport list in the Pretoria government archives, image group 008019246, carries THREE CONSECUTIVE BOOYZENS shipped on the CITY OF CAMBRIDGE on 3 JUNE 1901, all entered from PRETORIA: 18463 STEPHANUS FRANCOIS, 28 · 18464 PETRUS JACOBUS, 29 · 18465 DAVID SCHALK, 54. Consecutive numbers on one transport means taken together. Age 28 against this archive's c. October 1874, which would have made him 26. THE FULLER REGISTER WAS THEN FOUND, and it is better than the De List in every respect: item 1 of the same film, image 126, gives all three as living at PRETORIA, riding with the PRETORIA COMMANDO, and TAKEN AT TOLOSBERG ON 25 APRIL 1901. Its ages are 26, 27 and 53, which match this archive's own dates where the De List's 28, 29 and 54 did not. AND THEN THE PRISONER NUMBER LED SOMEWHERE ELSE ENTIRELY. The medal-roll database at angloboerwar.com holds an entry for a STEPHANUS FRANCOIS BOOYSEN, BURGER, whose PoW number is 18463 — the same number as the register — and it says he was a ZARP, one of the ZAR's police, based at PRETORIA. Quoting a City Coins auction catalogue of November 2020 that described his ABO medal and the papers with it: in action at TALANA, MODDER SPRUIT, COLENSO, PLATRAND (WAGON HILL) where he was WOUNDED IN THE RIGHT LEG ABOVE THE KNEE, SPION KOP and DALMANUTHA — the ZARPs' famous last stand. His applications were completed by his commanding officer, COMMANDANT J. P. DE LA C. SCHROEDER. He was one of FORTY-TWO Boers taken at Tolosberg in the Waterval Valley on 25 April 1901, with two guns and much stock, and was sent to INDIA. This archive has NOT seen the medal or the application; it is strong secondary evidence tied to the register by the number and not by the name. WHAT IT DOES TO THE DISPUTE: he is numbered 18463 and David Schalk Booysen is 18465, two apart on the same transport on the same day, and this man died at EAST LYNNE, PRETORIA, which is the district all three were taken in. That is a FOURTH point favouring David Schalk as his father, and the first that does not depend on a forename. It is still not a document naming a parent. PARENTAGE DISPUTED — see below. A son of the second marriage, and a MESSELAAR — a mason, like his half-brother Willem Hermanus at Indwe. His 1940 Sterfkennis was fetched because it should have named his mother; his widow wrote only “oorlede” for both parents. Married BEATRIX MAGDALENA CATHARINA BOSHOFF at Mosselbaai on 5 SEPTEMBER 1905, certificate 1318 — he 30 and a JONKMAN, she SIXTEEN with her parents consenting. Eleven children; left immovable property and a will. THE REGISTER GIVES HIS RESIDENCE AS PRETORIA, and eleven weeks later David Schalk Booijzen of Goede Hoop, Pretoria — whose 1900 notice names an unmarried major son called Stephanus François — remarried in that same city. This archive placed him under Petrus Jacobus on his birth year alone. It is marked SERIOUS on the disputed page and it is not decided.

people.b: 16 Jun 1889, baptised 16 Feb 1890 at Mossel Bay
people.r: HER HALF OF THE SILVERTON STONE READS: “AAN ONS DIERBARE MOEDER — BEATRIX MAGDALENA CATHARINA (GEB. BOSHOFF) — ✳ 18-7-1888, † 23-5-1977 — Deur Jesus was vrede behaal, sy kruisdood het alles betaal. Ges. 12:6”. THE DEATH IS NEW AND THE BIRTH DISAGREES WITH THIS ARCHIVE. Her baptism at Mossel Bay on 16 February 1890 gives her born 16 JUNE 1889; the stone says 18 JULY 1888, and the eGGSA index transcribes it 1889. A baptism register written weeks after the event outranks a stone cut eighty-eight years later, so this archive keeps 1889 — and records the disagreement rather than hiding it. BURIED AT SILVERTON, PRETORIA, on a joint stone with her husband: “nee BOSHOFF 1889-1977”. The birth year matches her 1890 Mossel Bay baptism and 1977 is a death year this archive did not have. IMAGE LOCATED, NOT YET READ. His widow, who signed the 1940 death notice at Pretoria on 26 July 1940 — and who could not name her husband's parents. SHE WAS SIXTEEN when she married him at Mosselbaai on 5 September 1905, with her parents consenting; he was thirty. Her own parents were EVERT PHILIP BOSHOFF and SUSANNA FREDERIKA ALETTA MEYER, named on her 1890 baptism — and two of her eleven children are called straight after them.

AND THE ESTATE INDEX AGREES WITH THE STONE, which is what moves him from inferred to documented: “MHG 7653/66 — BOOYZEN, DAVID SCHALK, 1966”. The stone gives an initial and a year; the estate index gives the name in full and the same year. Two collections that do not speak to each other, found an hour apart. OUBOET ON THE SILVERTON PILLAR, and now a grave: “BOOYZEN DAVID S. 1907–1966 & RACHEL M. 1909–1973”, Zandfontein cemetery, Pretoria. The initial, the forename, the town and a birth two years after his parents’ 1905 marriage all agree, and he is the only David S. Booyzen in the Gauteng collection. IT IS A MATCH ON A NAME AND A DATE, NOT A DOCUMENT, and it is marked inferred for that reason. FROM THE INDEX; no image read. Eldest named on his father's 1940 estate — and a name that matters. If Stephanus Francois is DAVID SCHALK BOOIJZEN's son, as the 1900 death notice suggests, then this boy is called after his grandfather outright. Under the reading this archive published instead, he is called after a great-uncle. It is a point in the argument and not a proof.
Married a Luus. Named for her mother's mother, SUSANNA FREDERIKA ALETTA MEYER — one of two children on this list called straight after the Boshoff grandparents.
Named for his mother's father, EVERT PHILIP BOSHOFF. The Boshoff grandparents are the only two people in this household whose names are accounted for without argument.

BESSIE ON THE SILVERTON PILLAR. The 1940 estate says only that she married a Bekker; the eGGSA index gives “BEKKER IGNATIUS MICHAEL 1908–1981 & ELIZABETHA MARGARETHA BOOYZEN 1909–1982” IN SILVERTON MAIN CEMETERY — the same ground as her parents. Name, surname of the husband, cemetery and a plausible birth all agree, and she is the only one in the collection. A MATCH, NOT A DOCUMENT. FROM THE INDEX; no image read.

BETIE ON THE SILVERTON PILLAR, AND THE ONLY ONE OF THE SIX MISSING CHILDREN WHO CAN BE FOUND. Her husband has a name: TAB MHG 4300/51 — “VERMEULEN, MICHAEL JOHANNES, 1951. PREDECEASED SPOUSE ELSIE KATRINA VERMEULEN. SURVIVING SPOUSE BEATRIX MAGDALENA CATHARINA VERMEULEN (BORN BOOYZEN).” So she was his SECOND wife, and SHE OUTLIVED HIM. Found not by looking for her but by putting VERMEULEN and BOOYZEN to the index together — the same relationship trick that opened the Kolbes. Named for her mother. THE ESTATE IS NOT READ.

HENNA ON THE SILVERTON PILLAR — the match this archive called the weakest of the nine, because Henna can stand for Hendrina as readily as for Johanna. The stone does not settle that, but it does find her: “DU PLESSIS GERHARDUS EBENHAEZER 1911–1988 & JOHANNA CATHARINA BOOYZEN 1913–1982”, Rebecca Street cemetery, Pretoria. The 1940 estate says she married a Du Plessis. A MATCH, NOT A DOCUMENT. FROM THE INDEX; no image read.

FANIE ON THE SILVERTON PILLAR. “BOOYZEN STEPHANUS FRANCOIS 1918–1991 & ELENA JACOBA HORN 1921–1989”, Silverton main cemetery — his parents’ ground, his father’s name entire, and a birth thirteen years into the marriage. A MATCH, NOT A DOCUMENT. FROM THE INDEX; no image read. Named for his father.

WILLIE ON THE SILVERTON PILLAR, and the weakest of the five matches made today: “BOOYZEN WILLIE 1920–2000 & ENID MOUTON 1926–2000” in Silverton main cemetery. The stone gives only the household name, which is the one thing that cannot distinguish him from a nephew — and a WILLIE BOSHOFF BOOYZEN 1962–1993 lies in the same cemetery carrying his grandmother’s maiden name, so there is more than one Willie there. THE CEMETERY AND THE DATE FIT AND NOTHING ELSE DOES. FROM THE INDEX; no image read.
The sixth Petrus Jacobus this archive has found in this family.
Named on the 1940 estate and nowhere else.
Named on the 1940 estate and nowhere else.

A TWELFTH CHILD, AND THE ONLY WORD CUT FOR HER OR HIM IS “BABA”. The centre pillar of the Silverton stone lists twelve children by their household names; the 1940 estate lists eleven by their registered ones; and when the two are set side by side EVERY ONE OF THE ELEVEN IS CLAIMED EXACTLY ONCE, leaving “✝ BABA” — a birth star, a cross, and no name — with nothing to match. Not on the estate because the child was already dead when it was written. NO DATE, NO SEX, NO NAME, NO ORDER beyond the stone's own. This archive has met the shape before: Joseph Heinrich Daschner's 1942 notice named eleven children and the Brixton register produced a twelfth. A death notice lists the living; a gravestone, cut by the family, lists the children.
Her father, named on her 1890 baptism at Mossel Bay with Susanna Frederika Aletta Meyer. Two of his grandchildren carry his names and hers.
Her mother, named on the 1890 Mossel Bay baptism. Her granddaughter Susanna Fredrika Aletta Booyzen carries all three of her names.

The eldest of the eight children on the 1863 death notice, and the only one entered as a Major. Estate TAB MHG 52653 — he ended in the Transvaal. WikiTree gives him a wife this archive did not have at all: JACOMINA JACOBA JANSEN VAN RENSBURG, married 12 FEBRUARY 1866 AT MIDDELBURG. FROM WIKITREE, NOT FROM A DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS READ, and the profile contradicts itself — its own source line dates that marriage 1899, not 1866. Recorded as a lead and not adopted.
Baptised at Barkly Oost 15 Sep 1889 with both maternal grandparents standing as godparents — and on the facing page of the same register, the Mountjoy baptism three weeks later.
Eldest of the Johannesburg family.
Second child. Birth date corrected from 1 October on her mother’s 1944 death notice.
Fourth child.

One profile holding two men — and on 14 September 2026 they came apart. THE YORKSHIRE MAN IS NOW A LIFE: born at WHITBY in 1796; resident at BILSDALE MIDCABLE when he took a licence on 2 October 1838 to marry MARGARET JACKSON of Beadlam at Helmsley; and in the 1851 census a SHIP OWNER at SHIP YARDS, RUSWARP, WHITBY, aged 55, married, head of his household — the ONLY John Barry of that age in the whole Yorkshire census. John Barry deaths are then registered in the WHITBY district in 1858 and in 1860. He outlived the Cape man, who died at de Bruins Poort in 1853, by at least five years. THEY ARE TWO MEN. What this archive still does not have is the Cape one: no birth, no arrival, no burial. And a caution worth keeping — a Whitby SHIP OWNER is exactly the kind of man whose son could be born AT SEA, which is what John Augustus Barry's death notice says of 1819. That coincidence is not evidence, and the censuses say it is not the same man.
His 1915 death notice types the birthplace as at sea and his mother as “born Neagle”. Cape Mounted Rifles.

people.v: Henry Jaonas Barry · Hennery James Berry (both 1848 index entries)
people.r: SETTLED, 14 September 2026, and it removes a candidate rather than adding one. The HENRY JAONAS BARRY who turned up on 13 September — “baptised at twenty years old” in 1868, and briefly a candidate for a tenth child — IS THIS MAN. The same event is indexed twice: once as Henry Jaonas Barry, baptism 13 Nov 1868, and once as HENNERY JAMES BERRY, baptism 13 Nov 1848. Same birth date of 13 July 1848, same parents, same collection, and FamilySearch attaches BOTH to one tree person, James Henry Barry 1848–1939. The volume decides the year on its own: the register is “GRAAFF-REINET. BAPTISM RECORDS 1846–1851”, and a baptism of 1868 cannot sit in a book that closes in 1851. So he was baptised at four months, not at twenty, AT GRAAFF-REINET — not at Cape Town or Tulbagh, which is what both index entries say for the place. The birth-spacing argument made against him held: his brother John Augustus II was born 13 March 1847 and he was born sixteen months later. THE IMAGE HAS BEEN LOCATED AND NOT READ — identifier apid:TH-909-70517-31299-17. Named on the 1915 death notice, which he swore himself. The index now dates him: born about 1847, dead at Barkly East on 23 June 1939, having outlived his father by thirty-six years. BUT THAT YEAR CANNOT STAND. His brother John Augustus Barry II was born 13 MARCH 1847 off a register, and “about 1847” here is not a date at all — it is an age worked back from the 1939 death. Two brothers cannot share it. A relationship search on his mother's surname turned up a HENRY JAONAS BARRY born 13 July 1848 and baptised at twenty, which is where a next child belongs; whether that is this man under a clerk's ear is UNPROVED and the register is unread.

Kathleen's brother. Signed his mother's 1915 death notice as "Son in whose house deceased died", at Manorowen, Barkly East. A Richard Peter Barry, plaasboer of Jerpoint, is on the Cape Rebel roll — same name, right region, identity not proven.

AND THE NAME IS IN A GOVERNMENT FILE, TWICE OVER, IN ONE LINE. SAB, VWR volume 2, reference B645/8/38, 1937: “AANSOEK DEUR PLAASEIENAAR BARKLY-OOS. RPK BARRY. BYWONER RPK BARRY (SEUN).” An application by a farm owner at Barkly East — R.P.K. BARRY — and the bywoner on the place is R.P.K. BARRY, HIS SON. TWO MEN OF THESE INITIALS AT BARKLY EAST IN 1937, one holding the land and one working it as a tenant, and the state file is between them. This archive cannot say which of the two is the man born in 1899 and does not guess. A BYWONER is not a labourer and not an owner; it is the word South Africa used in the 1930s for a white tenant farming another man's ground, and VWR is the Department of Social Welfare. THE FILE HAS NOT BEEN READ. CARRIES BOTH NAMES AT ONCE — Richard Pieter, for the Barry of Manorowen, and Kolbe, for the 1820 Settler family his great-grandmother married out of. NEW, AND HE CARRIES THE WHOLE ARGUMENT IN HIS NAME. “BARRY, HENRY JAMES KOLBE. BORN IN BARKLY EAST, CAPE PROVINCE. UNMARRIED. DECEASED ESTATE”, Pietermaritzburg Archives Repository, MSCE 2183/1958. HENRY JAMES is the Barry forename this archive has followed since 1848; KOLBE is the surname it has spent the project proving is the source of half the family's given names. HERE THEY ARE IN ONE MAN, born in this archive's own town, dying UNMARRIED in Natal in 1958 — so the names stop with him. He is the third Barry found carrying Kolbe as a forename, after Richard Pieter Kolbe Barry and Anton Rector Kolbe Barry. NO PARENTS NAMED; the estate is not read.

THE TENTH CHILD, FOUND BY READING 267 REGISTER IMAGES — and she has the same name as her sister. Burgersdorp doopregister, image group 008039088, image 427: born 10 JULY 1855, baptised 22 JULY 1855, father JOHN BARRY, mother MARGARET LOUISA KOLBE. FOUR YEARS LATER THE SAME PARENTS BAPTISED ANOTHER CATHARINA MARY SOPHIA at Dordrecht, born 4 August 1859 — the woman who married into the Booyzens and carried the name to Australia. TWO DAUGHTERS, ONE NAME, DIFFERENT BIRTHDAYS FOUR YEARS APART IN DIFFERENT TOWNS. A baptism is not done twice, so the ordinary reading is the ordinary Cape practice: THIS CHILD DIED, AND THE NAME WAS GIVEN AGAIN. This archive has no burial for her and states the death only as “before August 1859”. AND SHE EXPLAINS THE NAME TWICE OVER: the archive has already shown CATHERINE MARIA SOPHIA is a Kolbe name, off the 1848 godmother Catharine Sophia Maria Kolber. It was thought important enough to use, lose, and use again.
p: The register, read image by image

people.r: AND BY THE AFTERNOON THERE WAS A CANDIDATE FOR THE MISSING NAME. The Queenstown Free Press of 13 February 1884 marries “CHARLES ANDREW WERDMULLER, OF STEYNSBURG, SECOND SON OF THE LATE C.J.O. WERDMULLER, OF BURGHERSDORP” to Charlotte Anne Callaghan. A man born 14 February 1857 was twenty-seven that week. NOT PROVED: no document read here names Charles Andrew’s mother, and his father — or a man of exactly that name — married again at Burgersdorp in 1874. NAMELESS IN THE INDEX, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The same sweep that found the tenth Barry child turned up a second entry with an EMPTY NAME COLUMN: born 14 February 1857, baptised 10 April 1857 at Burgersdorp, mother AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE, father COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER. She is the Settler's fourth daughter, born at Graaff-Reinet in 1829 — and this is the first of her children this archive has ever seen. THE CHILD'S OWN NAME IS ON THE PAGE AND NOT IN THE INDEX, so no search will ever return it. The register image has not been read; only the index line.
p: The register, read image by image

people.v: almost certainly GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE, the Settler's twin son
people.r: A DATE FOR THE TWIN, IF IT IS HIM. The stone at PIET RETIEF reads “VADER EN MOEDER — G.A. KOLBE — GEB. 23 FEB. 1836 — OVERL. 7 JAN. 1913 — A.M. KOLBE — GEB. 4 MEI 1843 — OVERL. 21 SEP. 1907 — VAN HUN KINDERS”. The Settler's ninth and tenth children were TWINS born at BURGERSDORP IN 1836, Charlotte Felicia and George Augustus, and this archive has never had a day for either. A G.A. KOLBE BORN 23 FEBRUARY 1836 IS EXACTLY THE RIGHT MAN IN EXACTLY THE RIGHT YEAR — and it would date his twin sister too. IT IS INITIALS AND A YEAR, NOT A NAME AND A PARENT, and this archive has spent today being careful about exactly this. It would also give the OTHER George Augustus Kolbe — born Burgersdorp 2 October 1861, dead Standerton 1934, buried Wakkerstroom — a plausible father aged twenty-five, which is the shape the eastern Transvaal Kolbes have been missing.

On the same stone, and known by two initials only. If her husband is the Settler's twin son then she is a daughter-in-law of the 1820 Settler and this archive does not know her name. “VAN HUN KINDERS” — the stone was raised by their children, and it does not name them either.

“P.J. KOLBE — GEB. 1_ AUG. 1865 — OORL. 28 NOV. 1919 — RUS SAG.” The day of birth will not resolve on the photograph and is not guessed. A second Kolbe stone at Piet Retief, thirty years younger than the first; if G.A. of 1836 is the twin, this is very likely his son. NOTHING ON THE STONE SAYS SO.

people.v: “Jan” · JOHN GERSON ELIEZER KOLBE, in his obituary · Commandant Kolbe
people.r: THE SETTLER'S ELDEST CHILD, AND UNTIL TODAY A LINE IN A TABLE. His obituary — Grahamstown Journal, 15 April 1868, headed “DEATH OF COMMANDANT KOLBE” — gives the whole man. Born 7 JULY 1822; married 3 APRIL 1843 to ANNA JACOBA VAN DER MERWE; DIED 3 APRIL 1868, ON HIS WEDDING ANNIVERSARY, at the farm LEEUWBERG, of TYPHUS OR TYPHOID CAUGHT ON COMMANDO — “thus adding another to the long list of victims of our miserable war”. He had settled on KAALSPRUIT about 1850 and lies there — AND HE CONFIRMS THE FARM HIMSELF. A lost-property advertisement he placed in the Friend on 9 MARCH 1864 is signed “J.G.E. KOLBE, Kafferberg, Kaalspruit” (the address as the paper printed it). The Friend’s own obituary transcription reads “[Randspruit]”, bracketed by the transcriber as doubtful; the man’s own address settles it. THAT ADVERTISEMENT ALSO PUTS THE TWO BROTHERS IN ONE DOCUMENT: it concerns “a promissory note, date 9th March 1864, drawn by GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE in favor of J.G.E. KOLBE, payable 4 months after date for £154 Stg” — lost on the Market Square at Bloemfontein. HE LEFT A WIDOW AND TWELVE CHILDREN — “OF THE EIGHT SONS AND FOUR DAUGHTERS HE HAS LEFT BEHIND HIM”, which is the Friend of the Free State’s own wording and a count the Grahamstown reprint drops. Only one daughter was married and the youngest child was an infant; TWO SONS HAD BEEN SERVING WITH HIM IN THE FIELD and “proved themselves amongst the bravest of our burghers”. NONE OF THE TWELVE IS NAMED AND NONE IS IN THIS ARCHIVE. He was COMMANDANT OF THE DISTRICT, A JUSTICE OF THE PEACE, A DIRECTOR OF THE BLOEMFONTEIN BANK and a DEACON of the Dutch Reformed Church, and he had spoken in the VOLKSRAAD in May 1867. He had refused public life for twelve years after THE ABANDONMENT, having protested the British withdrawal and applied to SIR GEORGE CLERK for compensation for his land so that he might leave with the troops; failing that, “he, like many more, had to cast his lot with the Free State”. AND ON HIS DEATHBED, in full possession of his senses, he told the doctor and the others present THAT THIS STATE HAD TAKEN TOO MUCH LAND FROM THE BASUTOS, that he had always thought so and had said so in the Raad, and begged them to rescind the resolution and treat with the Governor for an equitable boundary.

people.b: 29 Sep 1817, a military post in what became British Kaffraria
people.d: 23 Feb 1872, the Modder River road, district Bloemfontein
people.r: THE SECOND HUSBAND, and the reason the Commandant's widow is filed under the wrong surname in the Free State estate index. LANDDROST OF BLOEMFONTEIN, son of DR PATRICK McCABE, a Staff-Assistant Surgeon attached to the British Army on the Cape Frontier; his mother ROSE died at Bloemfontein on 1 August 1858, aged 72 years 3 months and 8 days. He married Anna Jacoba van der Merwe about APRIL 1871 — “his second wife, about ten months since” — and was dead within fifteen months. ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF THE STATE'S INDEPENDENCE he had spent the day superintending the burghers' annual target shooting for the government prize; at a quarter past five he set off by spring-cart for the Diamond Fields meaning to sleep at his own farm “UITVLUGT” on the Modder River; at about half past seven, in deceptive moonlight and one hour's ride short of the farm of G.F. Enslin, the cart went into a sluit washed out by the rains. He was dead of heart disease that evening. HE LEFT FOUR SONS AND TWO DAUGHTERS OF HIS OWN AND “A LARGE FAMILY OF STEP-CHILDREN”, which is a newspaper counting the Commandant's twelve. His brother JOSEPH, the well-known trader and traveller, had died in the interior in December 1865; his brother JOHN died at Bloemfontein in 1860. He was buried on the Sunday afternoon at six o'clock, the coffin carried by the resident members of the Volksraad and the principal government officers, with the State President and upwards of two hundred walking behind.

THE FIRST OF THE TWELVE THIS ARCHIVE CAN PUT A HAND ON. The Free State criminal court, October 1868: a horse thief drove off three animals from the farm SPRINGFIELD, ward Upper Modder-river, district Bloemfontein — a black mare and foal belonging to “ANNA JACOBA VAN DER MERWE, WIDOW OF LATE J.G.E. KOLBE”, a blue schimmel mare and foal belonging to “JOHN KOLBE, JUN.”, and a chestnut riding horse belonging to a man named Jephts. SIX MONTHS AFTER HIS FATHER DIED HE IS HOLDING STOCK IN HIS OWN RIGHT BESIDE HIS MOTHER. He is named by initial and suffix only, and nothing else about him is known — but AN EIGHTH OF THE OBITUARY'S “EIGHT SONS” NOW HAS A DOCUMENT. In 1884 The Friend reported that the eldest son of “Mr. John KOLBE”, a boy of ten called LITTLE JANNIE, was struck dead by lightning on his father's farm five hours north of Bloemfontein; the Natal Witness index carries the same death and names the father GEORGE. Two papers, two fathers, and this archive will not choose.

SHE REMARRIED, AND HER SECOND HUSBAND IS WHY SHE WAS HARD TO FIND. The Free State archives hold her under a different surname: VAB MHG M777 — “MCCABE, ANNA JACOBA. NOOIENSVAN VAN DER MERWE. EGGENOTE JOHN GHERSON [KOLBE]”, 1896. WIDOWED IN 1868 WITH TWELVE CHILDREN AND DEAD TWENTY-EIGHT YEARS LATER AS MRS MCCABE. Her husband’s own estate is beside it — VAB MHG K71, “KOLBE, JOHN GERSON ELEAZAR. EGGENOTE ANNA JACOBA (GEBORE VAN DER MERWE)”, 1868. AND THE McCABE NAME IS ALREADY IN THIS ARCHIVE: a ROSA MAGDALENA KOLBE was baptised at Bloemfontein in 1890 to Frederik Fortuna Kolbe and MARIA PETRONELLA ELIZABETH ANTOINETTA MCCABE — a second Kolbe–McCabe marriage in the same small Free State world, and this archive does not yet know whether that is a coincidence. NEITHER ESTATE IS READ. M777 is the document that would name the twelve children. Married JOHN GERSON ELIEZAR KOLBE on 3 APRIL 1843 and was widowed on the same date twenty-five years later. She is the third van der Merwe to marry into these families. 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 — McCABE HAS A FIRST NAME, A BIRTH DATE AND AN OFFICE. He is FRANCIS McCABE, LANDDROST OF BLOEMFONTEIN, son of Dr Patrick McCabe, a Staff-Assistant Surgeon attached to the British Army on the Cape Frontier, born at one of the military posts in what is now British Kaffraria on 29 SEPTEMBER 1817. His obituary in The Friend says he “married his second wife about ten months since — THE WIDOW OF THE LATE COMMANDANT J.G.E. KOLBE, OF KAFIRBERG, NEAR THIS TOWN”, and he died suddenly of heart disease on the Modder River road on 23 FEBRUARY 1872, aged 54, leaving “a widow, four sons and two daughters, BESIDES A LARGE FAMILY OF STEP-CHILDREN”. SO: MARRIED 3 APRIL 1843, WIDOWED 3 APRIL 1868 WITH TWELVE CHILDREN, MARRIED AGAIN ABOUT APRIL 1871, WIDOWED AGAIN FIFTEEN MONTHS LATER, AND DEAD IN 1896 UNDER HIS NAME. For about eleven months there were eighteen children attached to one household. She was living at SPRINGFIELD, WARD UPPER MODDER-RIVER, DISTRICT BLOEMFONTEIN in October 1868, when a black mare and foal of hers were stolen — the court record that says so is the only document this archive has that shows her doing anything at all.

people.v: Werdmuller van Elgg · D’Elgg · C.J.O. Werdmuller of Burghersdorp
people.d: 1882 — death notice KAB MOOC 6/9/187, 4160; will MOOC 7/1/431, 102
people.r: HE IS IN THE CAPE ARCHIVES FROM 1854 TO 1882 AND HE DIED IN 1882, not merely “before February 1884”. Motions in the Supreme Court in 1854, 1855, 1872 and 1873; a trustee in other men’s insolvent estates; and in 1882, GSC 2/1/1/41 no. 60, “CHARLES ANDREW WERDMULLER AND COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER TRADING AS C.A. WERDMULLER AND COMPANY” — FATHER AND SON IN BUSINESS TOGETHER, in the year he died. His own death notice and will are both filed and neither is read. THE MAN THE SETTLER’S FOURTH DAUGHTER MARRIED, and until today a bracket after her name. He is at BURGERSDORP in April 1857, standing at a font with AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE. He is at Burgersdorp again on 7 JULY 1874, married BY SPECIAL LICENCE by the Rev. William Cromar to ELIZABETH JOHANNA CATHARINE VORSTER — and the Eastern Province Herald prints his name in full as COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER D’ELGG, which is the first time this archive has seen the von Elgg written by anyone but a genealogist. He is DEAD by February 1884, when his second son marries as the son of “the late C.J.O. Werdmuller of Burghersdorp”. WHETHER AUGUSTA LOUISA WAS DEAD BEFORE 1874 THIS ARCHIVE DOES NOT KNOW.

THE DATES NOW CLOSE AROUND HIM, THOUGH NO DOCUMENT YET NAMES HIS MOTHER. His father’s first wife, AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE, MADE A WILL IN 1868 AND DIED IN 1873 — KAB MOOC 7/1/332 no. 205, “KOLBE, AUGUSTA LOUISA, WIFE OF COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER VAN ELGG”, filed 1873 — and his father remarried on 7 JULY 1874. IN 1882 CHARLES ANDREW WAS IN BUSINESS WITH HIS FATHER as C.A. Werdmuller and Company, and in February 1884 he married. A SON OF THE 1874 MARRIAGE WOULD HAVE BEEN SEVEN AND NINE. He can only be a child of the first marriage, and the first wife is the Settler’s daughter. THE ONE LOOPHOLE LEFT is an earlier wife before Augusta Louisa, and his father’s 1882 DEATH NOTICE would close it by naming the children. SECOND SON OF THE LATE C.J.O. WERDMULLER OF BURGHERSDORP, married at Wesley Church, Queenstown, on 13 FEBRUARY 1884 to CHARLOTTE ANNE CALLAGHAN, eldest daughter of Hugh Callaghan of Ashby Manor. Of STEYNSBURG then, and by 1909 CHARLES WERDMULLER, J.P., OF HOOPSTAD in the Orange River Colony — the town his wife died in. HIS MOTHER IS NOT NAMED ON ANYTHING READ HERE. If he is the child born 14 February 1857 at Burgersdorp he is AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE’S SON and a grandson of the 1820 Settler; if he belongs to his father’s 1874 marriage he is no relation at all, and a man marrying in 1884 as a second son cannot be. THE DATES FAVOUR KOLBE AND THE DOCUMENTS DO NOT SAY IT.

THE SETTLER'S FOURTH DAUGHTER HAS THREE DOCUMENTS AND THIS ARCHIVE HAD NONE OF THEM. A WILL, MADE IN 1868 AND FILED IN 1873: KAB MOOC 7/1/332 no. 205, “KOLBE, AUGUSTA LOUISA. WIFE OF COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER VAN ELGG” — which is the first document read here that ties her to that man by anything but a newspaper. A DEATH NOTICE, MOOC 6/9/145 no. 9981, 1873. And a LIQUIDATION AND DISTRIBUTION ACCOUNT, MOOC 13/1/299 no. 93, 1874, which means there was something to distribute. SHE DIED IN 1873 AND HER HUSBAND REMARRIED IN JULY 1874 — a year and a month, which is what a widower does, and which settles the question this archive left open yesterday about whose son Charles Andrew is. NONE OF THE THREE IS READ.

THE FORTUNATUS NAME IN A FOURTH SURNAME. “PETITION OF FREDERICK FORTUNATUS WERDMULLER OF MALMESBURY”, Cape Supreme Court, 1907, twice in one year, both times in other men's insolvent estates; and an estate of his own in 1953. This archive has already followed FREDERIK FORTUNATUS from Kolbe (1839) to Barry (1863) to Booÿsen (1899); here it is again, on a Werdmuller — and Augusta Louisa Kolbe married a Werdmuller. NOT SHOWN TO BE HER DESCENDANT, and the name is not the kind of name that travels by accident.

people.d: 17 Feb 1891, Hoopstad, Orange Free State — aged 32
people.r: ELDEST DAUGHTER OF HUGH CALLAGHAN, ESQ., OF ASHBY MANOR, district of Queenstown; married Charles Andrew Werdmuller on 13 February 1884. SEVEN YEARS LATER SHE WAS DEAD AT THIRTY-TWO, at Hoopstad, “after a long illness”, and a correspondent’s obituary in the Queenstown Free Press adds that she had arrived there only a few months before, in indifferent health, with a disorder of the heart that proved organic. SHE LEFT “A HUSBAND AND TWO LITTLE GIRLS”, and it is that line which lets the 1909 marriage notice call Amy a second daughter.

“MARTINEAU — WERDMULLER — On July 31 [1909], at EAST LONDON, HORACE ROBERT MARTINEAU, V.C., of Durban, to AMY WERDMULLER, SECOND DAUGHTER OF CHARLES WERDMULLER, J.P. OF HOOPSTAD, O.R.C.” One of the two little girls her mother left in 1891. IF THE CHAIN HOLDS — and it has one unproved link, her grandmother’s name — she is a GREAT-GRANDDAUGHTER OF THE 1820 SETTLER, and she married a holder of the VICTORIA CROSS. This archive prints the two letters as the journal printed them and has NOT gone looking for which action he won it for.
Carries the Kolbe given name Fortunatus.
Godfather at the Burgersdorp font on 23 October 1853, standing for his sister Margaretha's son William Fredrik Barry. A brother this archive did not have.
Godfather at the same font, the same day. He carries his own father's name — George Augustus Kolbe, the 1820 Settler, dead at Colesberg nine years earlier.

people.v: Catharine Kolbe (1853) · Catharine Sophia Maria Kolber (1848)
people.r: SHE IS WHERE THE NAME COMES FROM, and this archive had her down as “Catharine Kolbe” and nothing more. On 13 November 1848 she stood godmother at Graaff-Reinet to her sister Margaretha's son HENRY JAMES BARRY, entry 603, and the clerk wrote her out in full: CATHARINE SOPHIA MARIA KOLBER. ELEVEN YEARS LATER her sister named a daughter CATHERINE MARIA SOPHIA — the Kathleen Barry who married into this family — and the name then ran through four more generations and three more surnames. This archive had called it a Barry name. It is a Kolbe name, and it belongs to a woman who never married into the Booyzens at all. She is also godmother at Burgersdorp in 1853, two entries above her sister Mary Elizabeth's son.

Married MARY ELIZABETH KOLBE, not Margaretha — and this archive took weeks and two documents to be sure of it. Named as the father on the Burgersdorp baptism of 23 October 1853, two entries above his sister-in-law's child.

people.v: Maria Elizabeth Kolbe, in her estate notice · Enslin
people.r: HER DEATH IS NOW DATED, AND SHE DIED WITHOUT A WILL. The Friend of the Free State, 23 October 1863, twice in two weeks: “Derwyl MARIA ELIZABETH KOLBE zonder testament na te laten is overleden en de nagebleven echtgenoot G.F. ENSLIN by brieve van administratie ter vereffening van haren boedel als executeur is aangesteld” — she had died INTESTATE and her husband was appointed executor of her estate. This archive had only “before 1867”, inferred. It is now BEFORE 23 OCTOBER 1863, from a notice her own husband placed. MARGARETHA'S SISTER, and the woman who married GEORGE FREDERICK ENSLIN — which is the whole answer to a contradiction this archive carried as Serious, that Margaretha appeared to marry Enslin while married to John Barry. It was resolved from Margaret Downing's 1867 death notice. The Burgersdorp register of 23 October 1853 shows it instead: the two sisters baptising a son each, two entries apart, on one page.
Her son, baptised on the same afternoon as his cousin William Fredrik Barry. Entered in the register as AUGUSTUS KOLBE, with the Enslin left off the child's own line entirely.

people.n: Anna van der Merwe of Burgersdorp
people.r: The third godparent at the 1853 Barry font, and the only one who is not a Kolbe. A VAN DER MERWE standing at a Barry christening at Burgersdorp — a surname this archive has been chasing on the entirely other side of the family, among the Booysens of Graaff-Reinet. Not connected, and set down so the coincidence is on the record.

Found twice in one day. He came in on the 1915 death notice of his mother Margaretha Kolbe, estate 1291, which names NINE children where his father's names eight — and then the Burgersdorp doopregister produced his baptism: WILLIAM FREDRIK, born 23 August 1853, christened 23 October, godparents JOHN KOLBE, ANNA VAN DER MERWE and GEORGE KOLBE. Two of the three are his mother's brothers. A SECOND William Frederick Thomas was baptised in 1861 and this archive cannot say whether the first died or a clerk erred — a doubt re-surfaced, and briefly mistaken for a new find, when the index was asked for every Barry child of a Kolbe mother. He is not on his father's notice, not on the Cape Rebel roll, and nowhere else in this archive. His father's 1903 registration said ELEVEN children; with William there are nine named and two still missing.

Wife of John Augustus Barry II and the mother of nine children baptised at Burgersdorp and Dordrecht between 1871 and 1889. This archive had John Augustus II as a name on two death notices with no wife and no children at all until the index was asked for every Barry child of a father called John Augustus. Her surname is spelled nine different ways across the entries — Ellinckhuizen, Ellinckhuisen, Elinchhiusen, Westerhuizen, Ellincahuyzen — and one son carries it as a forename. FROM THE INDEX.

THE THIRD OF THE NAME. Eldest child of John Augustus Barry II, and a niece of the Catherine Maria Sophia “Kathleen” Barry who married into this family — born twelve years after her aunt. The index enters her baptism at Graaff-Reinet on one record and Colesberg on another, from the same date. FROM THE INDEX.

The FOURTH John Augustus in four generations, and by 1908 at ELLIOT with a wife of his own, Maria Jacoba Gericke — the same village where Henry James Booyzen married Dorothea Regina Barry in 1912. FROM THE INDEX.
Carries her grandmother Margaretha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Kolbe's first two names. FROM THE INDEX.
His mother's surname given as a forename, which is how this archive knows the spelling mattered to the family even though no two clerks agreed on it. FROM THE INDEX.
Entered as Clarence Jongerheld on one record and Clarence Ingerheld on another. FROM THE INDEX.
Named for his uncle George Augustus Barry, who is himself named for George Augustus Kolbe. FROM THE INDEX.
THE KOLBE NAME IN A FOURTH GENERATION — carried by a great-grandson of the 1820 Settler, sixty-two years after the landing, and the furthest down this archive has traced it. FROM THE INDEX.
Named for her mother. The household has moved from Burgersdorp to Dordrecht by this baptism. FROM THE INDEX.
The ninth and last, and the only one the index gives no fuller name for. FROM THE INDEX.
Named on the 1915 death notice.

people.b: 13 Mar 1847, baptised 12 Apr 1847 at Graaff-Reinet, entry 80
people.r: THE ENTRY HAS NOW BEEN READ, film 008119684 image 876, and every witness at his font is a KOLBE: “Gt: JOHN KOLBE, MARGARET KOLBE, AUGUSTA KOLBE” — the third name is the least certain of the three. The clerk writes the child JOHN AUGUST and the mother MARGARETWINA KOLBE. Read beside his brother’s font of the following year, where the godmother is CATHARINE SOPHIA MARIA KOLBER, it makes one point twice: the forenames this archive has spent the project calling BARRY NAMES are Kolbe names, standing at Kolbe godparents’ fonts. The eldest son on the 1915 notice, carrying his father's name exactly — which is why this archive calls the father John Augustus Barry I. His own documents call him simply John Barry, and that is the third man in this family the name has to be shared out between. His birth date does one more job than it looks: being HARD, off a register, it is what forces his brother James Henry's “about 1847” to move.
NEW. Named on his father's 1915 death notice and nowhere else this archive has looked. He carries his grandfather George Augustus Kolbe's names entire.

Born Barry, and on the 1915 notice as married to Tom Bedford. The tree carries a Margaretha Louisa Maria who married Thomas Bedford in 1875; the notice gives her as Margaret Mary, and the archive has not reconciled the two.

people.v: John Gottlob · “JOHN GODLOFF KOLBE ESQ. OF BRUNSWICK-SQUARE”, in his son’s 1844 obituary
people.r: HE HAD EIGHT SONS, AND THIS ARCHIVE KNEW OF ONE. His son’s obituary in the Grahamstown Journal of 19 December 1844 calls George Augustus “THE LAST REMAINING OF EIGHT SONS OF JOHN GODLOFF KOLBE ESQ. OF BRUNSWICK-SQUARE, LONDON”. SEVEN BROTHERS, ALL DEAD BEFORE DECEMBER 1844, none of them named anywhere in this archive — and dead men do not appear in a census, which is why the 1841 Conduit Street household holds three women and no sons. THE OBITUARY ALSO PUTS HIM AT BRUNSWICK SQUARE, in Bloomsbury, where the census and the death put him at CONDUIT STREET in Mayfair, a mile and a half away. Both can be true twenty years apart, and this archive has already moved this man once — off the family tree’s Lamb’s Conduit Street — so it records a second address rather than making a second correction. “ESQ.”, not “tailor”. AND HE IS IN THE LONDON GAZETTE, nine years before he died: issue 19424, page 1702, 29 September 1836, dissolving the copartnership of “JOHN GOTTLOB KOLBE and DAVID FLETCHER, of Conduit-Street, Bond-Street, in the County of Middlesex, TAILORS”. That is his trade, his street and a business partner, in print, from a free source — and it pushes him back to Conduit Street in 1836. AND THE DEATH IS NOW A GRO REFERENCE: FreeBMD gives one Kolbe death in all of England and Wales for 1845–46 — “Deaths Dec 1845, KOLBE, JOHN GOTTLOB, ST GEO HAN SQ, VOL 1, PAGE 35”. The district matches the census; the name form JOHN GOTTLOB matches his son's 1803 baptism; and the certificate, not yet ordered, would name the informant. FOUND IN THE 1841 CENSUS, which settles two things this archive had argued from other documents. He is at CONDUIT STREET, St George Hanover Square, sub-district MAY FAIR, aged 76 — four years before he died at number 34, and independent of the death record that corrected the family tree's Lamb's Conduit Street. And his birth county is entered as “FOREIGN”, which is the first document in this archive to say in its own words that he was not English. HO107, piece 734, book 1, folio 11, page 15, SCHEDULE 38. Three women share that schedule: Marianne, 35, Charlotte, 30, and Amelia A., 25. Tailor. Died at 34 Conduit Street, Mayfair — not Lamb's Conduit Street; the tree's photograph is of the wrong building. Buried at the German Savoy Church, Strand.

Aged 35 and living with her father Johan Gottlieb in Conduit Street at the 1841 census, schedule 38. Almost certainly a sister of George Augustus, who had sailed for the Cape twenty-one years earlier and never came back. FROM THE CENSUS — no baptism has been read for her.
Aged 30 in the Conduit Street household at the 1841 census. FROM THE CENSUS.

Aged 25 in the Conduit Street household at the 1841 census, and the youngest of the three women there. AND SHE MARRIED: Amelia Ann Kolbe, at ST PANCRAS in 1854, indexed twice. The groom is not in the index this archive read and she is the only one of the three sisters who can currently be followed out of the house. FROM THE CENSUS AND THE MARRIAGE INDEX.

HIS OBITUARY IS FOUND, eighteen days after the death: Grahamstown Journal, 19 December 1844. “DIED at his Farm, Wirtemberg, near the Orange River, December 1st, THE REV. GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE, aged 44 years, a man possessed of a most amiable temper, and of more than ordinary abilities. HE WAS THE LAST REMAINING OF EIGHT SONS OF JOHN GODLOFF KOLBE ESQ. OF BRUNSWICK-SQUARE, LONDON, has left a WIDOW AND TEN CHILDREN... he having been for many years engaged in RENDERING THEM MEDICAL ADVICE AND ASSISTANCE whenever called upon... HIS DISEASE WAS AN AFFECTION ON THE LUNGS.” EIGHT SONS, seven of them dead before December 1844 and not one in this archive. BRUNSWICK SQUARE, which is not Conduit Street and is a mile and a half from it. A MAN WHO DOCTORED A DISTRICT FOR THIRTY YEARS, where his own death notice says only “Agriculturist”. And a cause of death, after nearly a year ill. The notice also says 44 when he was 41, and ten children when this archive counts eleven living — it is the best kind of source and it is not a register. 1820 Settler — the Nautilus, Owen's party, Algoa Bay 14 Apr 1820. Married at sixteen on a sworn falsehood. Preached across the Orange River. His grandson could not name him in 1915.

people.d: 2_ Nov 1867, Burgersdorp — the day illegible on the stone
people.r: THE ANSWER WAS ON A PHOTOGRAPH THIS ARCHIVE HAS HAD ALL ALONG. The Burgersdorp monument is on the Kolbe page, and the caption quoted it as far as “ALSO HIS RELICT MARGARET DOWNING…” AND STOPPED THERE. The stone goes on: “BORN IN LONDON 23 FEBRUARY 1803 AND DIED AT BURGHERSDORP 2_ NOVEMBER 1867.” HER BIRTH IS NOW A DATE — 23 February 1803, where this archive had “c. 1804” — AND THE DEATH IS SETTLED AT 1867. Her son’s obituary of 15 April 1868 said she had died “about three months since”, which would have been January 1868; it was nearly five months, and a journalist rounding is a journalist rounding. THE DAY IS A 2 AND A DIGIT THAT WILL NOT RESOLVE at any magnification, and is not guessed. The Cape estate ran on: MOOC 13/1/253 no. 2, “DOWNING, MARGARET, WIDOW OF KOLBE, GEORGE AUGUSTUS. LIQUIDATION AND DISTRIBUTION ACCOUNT”, 1869 — and she had made a WILL OF HER OWN in 1854, MOOC 7/1/295 no. 70, ten years after she was widowed. Married at fifteen in Shoreditch, signing with a mark. Died owning a house and a farm.
Margaret's father.
Of the London Kolbes.
Of the London Kolbes.
One of the five Kolbe children whose death records are not yet read.

THE SOURCE OF THE FORTUNATUS NAME across three families — and, as of 14 September 2026, A MAN WITH A HOUSEHOLD. The Settler's tenth child, born at a mission station the year his father was working the Orange River. He married ELIZABETH JOHANNA DU TOIT, and eight of their children are in the Dutch Reformed registers: baptised at COLESBERG in 1863, 1865, 1868, 1873, 1876 and 1877, at HOPETOWN in 1870, and at BETHULIE in 1881. The eldest is a GEORGE AUGUSTUS, named for the grandfather who had been dead nineteen years. THEN THE HOUSEHOLD GOES NORTH: three of those children marry or die at WAKKERSTROOM in the eastern Transvaal, four hundred miles from the font. That is the second proof of the Wakkerstroom convergence, and it does not depend on a name — it is a family moving.

people.v: Elizabeth Geertruida du Toit, once, at the Hopetown font in 1870
people.r: FREDERIK FORTUNATUS KOLBE'S WIFE, and the mother of the Settler's Colesberg grandchildren — a woman this archive did not know existed until the index was asked for a relationship rather than a person. She is named at eight fonts across eighteen years and three churches, and her name holds steady at every one but Hopetown. NOT YET FOUND: her marriage, her parents, her death.

THE SETTLER'S GRANDSON, CARRYING HIS NAME ENTIRE, and the man the Wakkerstroom Kolbes descend from. Baptised at Colesberg in the year of his uncle Frederick Fortunatus Barry's birth. Married MARTHA SOPHIA KLOPPER, who was seventeen, about 1885; their eldest, Maria Johanna, was born at Wakkerstroom in 1886. AND HIS STONE SETTLES THE IDENTIFICATION BEYOND ARGUMENT: “VADER — GEORGE AUGUSTUS — GEB. 29 JULIE 1863 — OORL. 28 SEPT. 1954”, which is the COLESBERG FONT DATE TO THE DAY. The 1902 POW record with residence Wakkerstroom is NOT HIS: the other George Augustus Kolbe of that town was born 2 October 1861 and was exactly forty through ten months of 1902, where this one was thirty-nine. Died at Wakkerstroom on 28 September 1954, aged 91, which counts EXACTLY from the Colesberg font: born 29 July 1863, dead 28 September 1954. He outlived two of his sons by thirty-six years.

HER HALF OF THE STONE: “MOEDER — MARTHA SOPHIA (GEB. KLOPPER) — GEB. 27 MEI 1867 — OORL. 14 OKT. 1950 — Ons dank God elke maal as ons aan haar dink.” The birth is new; the death matches the civil register to the day. Married George Augustus Kolbe of Wakkerstroom AT SEVENTEEN, about 1885 — the fourth bride in this archive married before eighteen, and the third in the Kolbe line. Named as the mother on her daughter Maria Johanna's 1953 estate file, which is how this archive learnt she existed. She died four years before her husband.

THE SECOND GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE OF WAKKERSTROOM, and the reason this archive had to withdraw a claim within the hour. His stone: “IN LIEFVOLLE HERINNERING AAN ONS OUERS — GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE — GEB. 2 OKTOBER 1861 — OORL. 8 NOVEMBER 1934 — EN SUSANNA MARGARETHA KOLBE — GEB. 26 OKTOBER 1861 — OORL. 28 JULIE 1940 — HULLE RUS.” BORN AT BURGERSDORP, which is where the 1820 Settler is buried and where the Settler's twin son George Augustus was born in 1836; the descent is not documented here and is not claimed. He is buried at WAKKERSTROOM although he died at Standerton, in the same cemetery as the other man of his name, TWO YEARS APART IN BIRTH AND TWENTY IN DEATH. AND THE BIRTH DATE DECIDES THE PRISONER: the 1902 POW record of WO 108/368 gives a George Augustus Kolbe of Wakkerstroom AGED 40, and a man born 2 October 1861 was forty from October 1901 to October 1902, where the other was thirty-nine all year. THE PRISONER IS THIS MAN.

people.v: Susanna Margaretha Kolbe, on the stone
people.r: His wife, named on the Free State Dutch Reformed marriage register — he 27, residence WAKKERSTROOM — and on the Wakkerstroom stone beside him, born the same year as her husband to within three weeks. The Transvaal probate index also holds a SUSANNA MARGARETHA DOWNING KOLBE, unattached, which would make a second carrier of the London surname; this archive cannot yet say whether that is her daughter or another woman.
Second of the eight. The only one of his generation whose forenames come from neither the Kolbes nor the Downings — a du Toit name, presumably, off his mother's side. NOT FOLLOWED OUT OF THE FONT.

Third of the eight. Her name is the one that then travels: an ANGELINE KOLBE dies at Wakkerstroom in 1900 and a MARTHA ANGELINE KOLBE is buried at Volksrust in 1901, aged two months. Neither can yet be attached to her, and this archive will not guess. NOT FOLLOWED OUT OF THE FONT.

Fourth of the eight, and the only one baptised at Hopetown — the register there calls her mother Elizabeth GEERTRUIDA du Toit, which is the single wobble in eight entries. SHE IS ALSO THE FIRST OF THE EIGHT TO SURFACE IN THE TRANSVAAL: a Margaret Harriet Kolbe, aged 24, marries DIRK JACOBUS ASPHELING VAN DER SPUY at Wakkerstroom. Her name is her aunt's — Harriet Hachilah Machilah, born at Philippolis in 1831.
Fifth of the eight. Two aunts' names run together: CATHERINE MARIA SOPHIA, born 1825, and AUGUSTA LOUISA, born 1829. NOT FOLLOWED OUT OF THE FONT.

Sixth of the eight, named for her mother exactly. AND SHE MARRIES AT WAKKERSTROOM: Elizabeth Johanna Kolbe, aged 21, to JOHN CHARLES PATTISON — the ages agree with the font to the year. The second of her father's children to be found in the eastern Transvaal.

SHE MARRIED A BEUKES AND DIED IN NATAL, and this archive had her file days before it knew who she was. “BEUKES, PETRONELLA JACOBA ADRIANA, BORN KOLBE, BORN IN COLESBERG”, Pietermaritzburg deceased estates — recorded here on 12 September as one of “two Kolbe-born women of Colesberg with estate files, neither in this archive”. On 14 September the relationship search gave her a father, a mother and a font, AND THE FONT SAYS COLESBERG, which is what her own estate says eighty-two years later. Seventh of the eight, and the last baptised at Colesberg. THE ESTATE IS NOT READ.

SHE MARRIED PIERRE FRANCOIS OOSTHUIZEN, WHO WAS BORN AT COLESBERG — his estate, NAB MSCE 414/1960, names her as his spouse, “ADRIANA HENRIETTA JOHANNA, BORN KOLBE”. Like her sister Petronella, she was sitting in this archive’s own search log two days before she had a family. THE ESTATE IS NOT READ. Youngest of the eight — and baptised at BETHULIE, the Orange Free State mission station where her father had himself been born forty-two years earlier. The family goes back to the same font in the next generation. NOT FOLLOWED OUT OF THE FONT.

people.v: Maria Johanna Kolbe van der Merwe
people.r: HER STONE IS READ AND IT NAMES HER CHILDREN THE WAY THIS FAMILY ALWAYS DOES. “IN LIEFDEVOLLE HERINNERING AAN ONS MAMMIE — MARIA JOHANNA VAN DER MERWE (GEB. KOLBE) — 26 OKT. 1886 – 1 OKT. 1953 — Wat hy doen is wel gedaan.” And underneath, six household names: MARTZI · P.S. · JUDIE · PIETMAN · CHARL EN SUZAN. THE BIRTH IS NOW A DATE — 26 October 1886, where this archive had only the year — and THE SIX CHILDREN ARE NEW. This is the THIRD stone in this archive to list children by what they were called rather than what they were registered as: the Booyzens at Silverton, the Kolbes at Wakkerstroom, and now this. BORN AT WAKKERSTROOM AND DEAD AT WAKKERSTROOM, sixty-seven years apart, in a town her grandfather had never seen. Her 1953 estate file is the document that names the whole household: FATHER George Augustus Kolbe, MOTHER Martha Sophia Klopper, HUSBAND Charl Daniel van der Merwe. Her birthplace is entered as “Wakkerstroomn, Transvaal, Blanke Unie-burger” — the clerk's spelling, and the Union's category.

people.v: Frederik Fortunetus Daomig Kolbe, on his own marriage entry
people.r: THE MAN WHO PROVED THE CONVERGENCE. He carries BOTH of this family's Kolbe names at once — FREDERIK FORTUNATUS off his grandfather, DOWNING off a London marriage of 1819 — and a London surname has no business in the eastern Transvaal except through that wedding. Born seventy-two years after it. Married HESTER GERBINA SUSANNA JOUBERT at Volksrust at twenty-one, the clerk writing his second name as “Daomig”. Dead at Wakkerstroom on 2 November 1918, four months after his brother Daniel, which is the influenza.

His death registration carries the words “G A KOLBE'S SON”, mangled by the index into “G A Kolbelsson” — and that is the line that ties the 1918 graves to the old man who outlived them by thirty-six years. Dead at twenty-five, four months before his brother Freddie. The stone at Wakkerstroom reads DAAN 1893–1918.

A WOMAN OF THIS NAME DIES AT WAKKERSTROOM IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WAR, and this archive cannot say who she is. Twenty-eight years old, female, surname Kolbe, registered at Wakkerstroom on 15 November 1900. SHE IS NOT THE VOLKSRUST CAMP GRAVE: that is a G.E. Kolbe aged 35, a different age in a different year in a different place, and the camp was barely open in November 1900. She is not on the list of Frederik Fortunatus's eight children either — too young for Martha Angelina of 1868, too old for Catharina Maria Louisa of 1873. A daughter-in-law, most likely. THE RECORD NAMES NO PARENTS, NO HUSBAND AND NO CAUSE.

IT STANDS IN WAKKERSTROOM MAIN CEMETERY, NOT AT VOLKSRUST. The index this archive read gives her burial as “Volksrust, Eastvaal District Council” — which is the DISTRICT, not the town, and Wakkerstroom lies inside it. WITH THE TOWN GOES THE CAMP: a family stone in a town churchyard, in Dutch, cut by a monumental mason twenty-five miles away in Natal, is not a camp burial, and this archive should not have gone near the word.
